title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): f: X → S, and quasi-coherent modules with connection or stratification relative to S. 'Trivial' means E ≅ f*F. 'Integrable' means trivial étale-locally. In characteristic p with a local p-base, integrable is equivalent to curvature and p-curvature both vanishing, which is equivalent to Frobenius descent (Cartier).

This page, item 3:
- Let G be a group over S. The image suggests 'étale', since 'fini' is struck out and the word read as 'lisse' is doubtful.
- Let P be a right G_X-torsor on X, and F a coherent S-module with a G-action.
- Then G_X acts on F_X = f*F. Because the sections of an étale group over étale X-schemes are locally constant, this action preserves the canonical (trivial) connection, and in fact the canonical stratification.
- Modules with integrable connection (or stratification) on étale X-schemes form a stack by étale descent. F_X, with its G_X-action, is therefore a G_X-equivariant object of this stack.
- One can then twist it by P. The result is P ×^{G_X} F_X, a module with integrable connection; the margin says integrable stratification, which coincides with integrable connection only for X smooth in characteristic 0.
- In modern terms this is the tensor functor Rep(G) → Strat(X/S) attached to an étale torsor, i.e. the 'associated stratified bundle'. Grothendieck calls it a universal way of producing integrable stratifications.

The Tannakian statement:
- Take S = Spec k, X geometrically connected and locally of finite presentation over k, with a rational point x.
- One should be able to form a 'strict' generalized group Π_1(X,x). The parentheticals say it is not necessarily reduced/perfect when X is not normal/étale(?).
- The category of modules with integrable stratification on X should be equivalent to finite-dimensional linear representations of Π_1(X,x).
- This is the stratified fundamental group scheme, the Tannaka dual of Strat(X). The étale fundamental group appears as the quotient obtained from finite étale torsors via the construction above.
- The page ends by announcing a generalization to an arbitrary base S. The next page develops it with a set L of primes, sections or radicial multisections Σ, and pro-étale groups Π with pro-torsors whose geometric fibres are quotients of the fundamental group: a relative stratified/Nori-type fundamental group.
errors: If G is read as 'lisse' (smooth) rather than 'étale', the claim that G_X preserves the canonical connection of F_X is false. A section g of G over U acts by a non-constant matrix, so ∇(gs) = dg·s + g∇s ≠ g∇s in general. Example: G = G_m, where the associated line bundles need not admit connections. The statement holds for G étale (locally constant sections), which matches the image and the struck-out 'fini'.
'G_X considéré comme faisceau sur S' should presumably be 'sur X' (or G as a sheaf on S acting through f*); as transcribed it is incoherent.
The Tannakian equivalence is stated as a conjecture ('doit être'). The parenthetical claims about non-reducedness/non-perfectness for non-normal or non-smooth X are not justified on the page.

ideas.what: Twisting the trivially-connected module F_X by an étale G_X-torsor to produce a module with integrable connection/stratification: the tensor functor Rep(G) → Strat(X/S).
ideas.modern_name: Associated stratified (flat) bundle of an étale torsor; contracted product P ×^G F
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; Gieseker (1975) in char p; dos Santos (2007)
ideas.where_published: The twisting/contracted product formalism is in SGA1 and Giraud; this specific use for stratifications: unsure

ideas.what: Integrable stratifications on a connected k-scheme with rational point should form a Tannakian category equivalent to Rep of a generalized fundamental group Π_1(X,x), defined even for non-smooth X.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972, Tannakian categories); Gieseker (1975); dos Santos (2007); Esnault–Mehta (2010)
ideas.where_published: Ideas transmitted via Saavedra's thesis (Grothendieck's student); not in EGA/SGA as such

ideas.what: Remark that the strict group need not be reduced/perfect when X is not normal/smooth, implicitly suggesting it is so in the smooth case.
ideas.modern_name: For smooth X in char p, all algebraic quotients of π^strat are smooth ('perfect' group scheme)

ideas.what: Announced generalization to arbitrary base S (continued next page with L-groups and pro-étale strict groups).
ideas.modern_name: Relative stratified / relative Nori fundamental group schemes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Later work on relative fundamental group schemes (various, 2000s–2010s)

missed.claim: Grothendieck (c.1972) sketches a Tannakian 'strict' fundamental group for integrable stratifications on arbitrary (possibly non-normal, non-smooth) geometrically connected k-schemes of finite presentation with a rational point. He notes the group may fail to be reduced/perfect outside the normal/smooth case. The literature (dos Santos, Esnault et al.) mostly treats smooth X; the singular/non-normal behaviour of π^strat is less developed.
missed.quote: on peut former le groupe strict ... (pas nécessairement parfait si X n'est pas ét.) Π_1(X,x), et la catégorie des Modules à stratifications intégrables sur X doit être équivalente à celle des représentations linéaires de dim finie du groupe généralisé Π_1(X,x)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Anticipates dos Santos' perfectness result for smooth X, and points to the stratified fundamental group of singular schemes as a natural object.

missed.claim: Program to extend the stratified Tannakian group to an arbitrary base S, with stratified modules relative to S as representations of a relative pro-group.
missed.quote: On doit pouvoir généraliser au cas d'une base quelconque S
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relative stratified fundamental groups over general bases are only partially developed.

deep.surprise_reason: The material anticipates the stratified fundamental group scheme (dos Santos 2007) and Gieseker-type questions around 1972, including a hint about non-perfectness for non-smooth X. However, these ideas are known to have circulated via Saavedra and Grothendieck's school, and the page is a sketch.
transcription_corrections: 'Soit G un groupe [-fini-] lisse[?] sur S': the image appears to read 'étale' ('ét.'), not 'lisse'.
'sur des schémas lisses[?] des schémas[?] étales[?] de X' is likely 'sur des X-schémas étales' or 'sur des schémas étales de X'.
'(considéré comme faisceau sur S)' should probably be read 'sur X'.
'(qui est proréd.[?] parfois si X n'est pas normal)' is uncertain; possibly 'pas nécessairement réduit si X n'est pas normal'.

Margin: 'Ce qu'on trouve ici, par le même argument, une stratification intégrable sur P^{G_X}F_X. Cela revient au cas où X est lisse et S de car. 0' is likely 'Cela revient au même si X est lisse et S de car. 0'.
